To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
a hybrid aqueous zinc ion capacitor (ZIC) comprising a zinc anode and an oxidized carbon nano tube (oCNT) cathode was developed.
the aqueous hybrid ZCIs with the oxidized CNT cathodes have shown a specific capacitance as high as 53 F g−1 and a stable cycle performance of 5000 cycles.

the surface oxygen groups of oCNTs play an important role for the reversible cation adsorption on oCNTs and the hybrid ZIC with the oCNT cathodes showed a stable cycling performance and high energy density.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a new type of aqueous metal ion capacitors, which is based on a novel electrode material, oxidized carbon nanomaterials.
the surface-enabled ZICS and provides an alternative strategy to design aqueous metal-ion capacitors

the development of a new aqueous hybrid capacitor with the surface-enabled cation adsorption mechanism and the Zn2+ shuttling chemistry, and the oCNT cathodes are demonstrated to be a promising electrode material for aqueous metal ion capacitors.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the surface chemistry of oCNTs is the key for the pseudocapacitance and the hybrid aqueous ZIC can be an excellent energy storage device.
the surface oxygen groups on the CNTs are responsible for the pseudocapacitance of the ZIC and the Faradaic reactions at the oCNT electrode contribute significantly to the energy storage of the ZIC.
the surface functional groups on the carbon materials play a crucial role in the performance of metal-ion capacitor.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the surface functional groups of the oCNTs are responsible for the pseudocapacitance behavior of ZIC, which is a new strategy to improve the energy density of the metal ion capacitor.

the ZIC with the oCNT cathodes is an alternative to the aqueous hybrid supercapacitors with the activated carbons and metal oxides, which are currently the most widely studied electrode materials for the supercapacitor.
the aqueous hybrid metal ion capacitor is promising for the next generation of energy storage devices.

the surface chemistry of the cathode plays a key role in the ZIC performance, and the ZIC can be further optimized by the surface engineering of the carbon cathode. The
the ZIC can be used as an energy storage device with high specific capacitance and good cycle stability.
